sections.content:
29,845 people

were counted on the census as "groundsmen and greenkeepers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Groundsmen and greenkeepers cut and lay turf and maintain areas for golf courses and other sports grounds.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "groundsmen and greenkeepers" there were more men than women (97.5% compared with 2.5%).

This means "groundsmen and greenkeepers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled agricultural and related trades".

Men made up 97.5% and women made up 2.5% of "groundsmen and greenkeepers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "groundsmen and greenkeepers" included:

  • sheet metal workers
  • vehicle paint technicians
  • tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "groundsmen and greenkeepers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "groundsmen and greenkeepers", 11.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "groundsmen and greenkeepers" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "groundsmen and greenkeepers" included:

  • boat and ship builders and repairers
  • weighers, graders and sorters
  • metal working production and maintenance fitters

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "groundsmen and greenkeepers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "groundsmen and greenkeepers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "groundsmen and greenkeepers", 9.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (85% compared with 15%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (87.1%) than self-employed (12.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
